controls.guidance: probe-iac and probe-app-chart check security groups and NSGs, private endpoints, public exposure of storage and databases, WAF placement and CIS benchmark configuration; runtime-probe-network-perimeter verifies exposure from outside; probe-cicd-env and probe-sdlc verify that infrastructure and application changes pass approval gates before apply or deploy.
evidenceExpected: Network security configuration (segmentation, private endpoints, WAF) for cloud workloads
Cloud configuration posture results against a benchmark
Change approval records for cloud infrastructure and applications

controls.title: Define minimum cloud monitoring and assess CSP information security capability
controls.prose: REs must define minimum monitoring requirements for the cloud environment and assess the CSP's information and cyber security capability, including that the CSP maintains an information security policy framework commensurate with its exposure, keeps its capability current as vulnerabilities, threats, assets and business environment change, tests its controls at a nature and frequency commensurate with the materiality of the service and the threat environment, and assesses its sub-contractors for confidentiality, integrity and availability of shared data.
controls.guidance: Evidence a cloud monitoring baseline (e.g. CloudTrail or Activity Log in all regions, GuardDuty or Defender for Cloud or Security Command Center enabled, config-change alerts) verified by probe-iac, plus the CSP assessment drawn from assurance reports and sub-processor lists in the vendor file.
evidenceExpected: Documented minimum cloud monitoring requirements and their implementation
CSP information security capability assessment including control-testing frequency and sub-contractor assessment

controls.title: Integrate CSP logs into the RE SOC or retain them in cloud for incident handling
controls.prose: The RE must ensure appropriate integration of logs and events from the CSP into its SOC wherever applicable, and/or retention of relevant logs in the cloud, for reporting and handling incidents affecting cloud-deployed services.
controls.guidance: probe-iac verifies log sinks (organisation trails, diagnostic settings, log router) and retention; runtime-probe-prod-env confirms events arrive in the SIEM. Retention length follows CERT-In Directions (180 days within Indian jurisdiction) and the RE's policy; the MD sets no number.
evidenceExpected: CSP audit and security log forwarding into the RE SIEM/SOC
Cloud log retention configuration
SOC use cases covering cloud control-plane events

controls.title: Continuous security patching of cloud-hosted applications and platforms
controls.prose: The RE's own application security must be complemented by the CSP's cyber resilience controls, and the CSP and RE must ensure continuous and regular updates of security software, including upgrades, fixes, patches and service packs, to protect applications from advanced threats and malware.
controls.guidance: Check managed-service versions (Kubernetes control plane, database engines, runtime images) for end-of-support, auto minor-version upgrade settings, node image age and base-image CVEs; patch timelines follow sdlc/policy.json dependencyPolicy.vulnerabilitySlaDays and the sla-table topic 'patch-sla'.
evidenceExpected: Patch and upgrade status of managed services and images
Vulnerability remediation within the RE's patch SLA

controls.title: CSP runs structured, threat-intelligence-driven vulnerability management
controls.prose: REs must ensure CSPs have a well-governed and structured approach to managing threats and vulnerabilities, supported by industry-specific threat intelligence.
controls.guidance: Evidence from CSP assurance reports (vulnerability management controls tested), CSP security bulletins subscribed to by the RE, and integration of CSP threat findings into RE workflows. RE-side vulnerability scanning of its own cloud workloads is evidenced under App-I.6(f).
evidenceExpected: CSP vulnerability and threat management description or tested assurance control
Subscription to CSP security advisories and threat intelligence feeds

controls.title: Business continuity for cloud disasters and CSP failure
controls.prose: The RE's business continuity framework must ensure it can continue critical operations with minimal disruption, and with integrity and security, if a disaster affects its cloud services or the CSP fails.
controls.guidance: probe-iac checks cross-region backups, replicas and infrastructure-as-code reproducibility; evidence failover runbooks and, for critical functions on a single CSP, a documented fallback (second region, second CSP or on-premises).
evidenceExpected: BCP scenarios for cloud region outage and CSP failure
Cross-region or cross-provider recovery design and tested runbooks

controls.title: CSP demonstrates cyber resilience including DR drills at multiple levels
controls.prose: REs must ensure the CSP has demonstrable preparedness for cyber resilience for the cloud services in use, systematically ensured through robust incident response and recovery practices, including DR drills at various levels of cloud service with necessary stakeholders.
controls.guidance: Evidence DR drill reports that include the CSP (region failover, backup restore, SaaS tenant recovery), with RTO and RPO achieved against targets (sla topic 'dr-drill').
evidenceExpected: DR drill reports for cloud services involving the CSP and stakeholders
CSP incident response and recovery capability evidence

controls.title: Cloud exit strategy covers data return, portability, secure purge and transition
controls.prose: Appendix I paragraph 8 lists points that may be evaluated when developing a cloud exit strategy. The binding element is 8(a): the SLA and exit strategy shall factor in agreed processes and turnaround times for returning the RE's service collaterals and data, data completeness and portability, secure purge of RE information from the CSP environment, smooth transition of services, and unambiguous liabilities, damages, penalties and indemnities. The remaining points are recommendations: the exit plan should track the evolving application design and delivery stack; contractually agreed exit and termination plans should specify how services and data will move out with minimal business impact while preserving integrity and security; and all transaction records, customer and operational information and configuration data should be taken over systematically, purged at the CSP end, and independent assurance obtained before sign-off.
controls.guidance: mandatory rests on 8(a) ('shall factor in'): a finding at defaultSeverity requires a missing or deficient data-return, portability, purge, transition or liability element in the SLA or exit strategy. Gaps against 8(b)-(d) (exit plan tracking the stack, contractual exit plan detail, systematic take-over with independent purge assurance) are recommendations under the MD and should be recorded at a lower severity or as observations; the successor NBFC Directions 2025 para 97(xvi) makes all four points part of a 'shall' exit strategy. Evidence a cloud exit plan per CSP with data export formats (open formats, database dumps, object storage copies), turnaround times, portability of IaC and container images, purge certification and independent assurance at sign-off. Heavy reliance on proprietary managed services with no portability analysis is recorded as a risk.
evidenceExpected: Cloud exit plan with data return turnaround, portability and purge procedures
SLA exit stipulations covering liabilities and penalties
Independent assurance of purge at the CSP before sign-off for completed exits

controls.title: Cloud audit and assurance scope
controls.prose: Audits, periodic reviews and third-party certifications for cloud usage should cover, as applicable, the roles and responsibilities of the RE and CSP in cloud governance, access and network controls, configurations, monitoring, data encryption, log review, change management, incident response, and resilience preparedness and testing.
controls.guidance: Check the scope section of cloud audit reports and CSP certifications against this list; Maxwell probe observations for IAM, network, configuration, encryption, logging and change management can be attached as supporting evidence but do not replace the independent audit. Recorded as non-mandatory because the MD says the audit scope 'should cover' these areas; defaultSeverity is indicative only. The successor NBFC Directions 2025 para 97(xvii) ('shall ... ensure that the audit / periodic review / third-party certifications cover') makes it binding for entities under the successor Directions.
evidenceExpected: Cloud audit or review report with scope covering the listed areas
Third-party certifications of the CSP with relevant scope

groups.title: Appendix II: Outsourcing of Security Operations Centre

controls.title: Identify the owner of assets used in outsourced SOC services
controls.prose: Because outsourced SOC operations store and process data externally under a Managed Security Service Provider with less RE visibility, REs outsourcing SOC operations must, in addition to the other controls, unambiguously identify the owner of the assets used to provide the service, including systems, software, source code, processes and concepts.
controls.guidance: Applies when details.json socModel is 'managed-soc' or a vendor has a 'security-operations' service. Expect an asset-ownership schedule in the MSSP contract (SIEM licences, collectors, playbooks, detection content, dashboards).
evidenceExpected: Asset ownership schedule for the outsourced SOC in the MSSP contract

controls.title: RE owns and oversees SOC rules, customisation, logs and analytics
controls.prose: REs must have adequate oversight and ownership of rule definitions, customisation and the related data, logs, metadata and analytics specific to the RE.
controls.guidance: Evidence RE admin or read access to the SIEM content repository, exportable detection rules (e.g. Sigma or native format) and logs, and a change log of rule changes approved by the RE. runtime-probe-identity-access can confirm RE-held roles on the SIEM or XDR tenant.
evidenceExpected: RE access to and ownership of SIEM rules, customisations, logs and analytics
Export of RE-specific detection rules and change history approved by the RE

controls.title: Periodically assess SOC functioning including physical facilities
controls.prose: REs must periodically assess the functioning of the outsourced SOC, including all physical facilities involved in service delivery such as the SOC itself and areas where client data is stored or processed.
controls.guidance: Evidence periodic site assessments or audits of the MSSP SOC and data-processing locations, and SOC performance metrics (mean time to detect and respond, alert backlog, coverage of log sources).
evidenceExpected: Periodic assessment or audit report of MSSP SOC operations and facilities
SOC performance metrics reviewed by the RE

controls.title: Integrate outsourced SOC reporting and escalation with RE incident response
controls.prose: REs must integrate the outsourced SOC's reporting and escalation process with the RE's incident response process.
controls.guidance: Check the incident response plan names the MSSP escalation path, severity mapping and hand-off, and that SOC-originated incidents in the ledger show RE-side triage times compatible with 17(h) and CERT-In 6-hour reporting.
evidenceExpected: Incident response plan showing MSSP escalation integration
Records of SOC-escalated incidents handled through the RE process

controls.title: Review the outsourced SOC's alert and event handling process
controls.prose: REs must review the process by which the outsourced SOC handles alerts and events.
controls.guidance: Evidence periodic sampling of closed alerts for correct triage, false-positive tuning reviews, and SLA compliance for alert acknowledgement and escalation.
evidenceExpected: Alert-handling review reports with sampled alerts and outcomes
SOC alert SLA compliance report

groups.title: Appendix III: Services not considered under Outsourcing of IT Services

controls.title: Services and activities outside the scope of IT outsourcing
controls.prose: Indicative, non-exhaustive list of services not treated as Outsourcing of IT Services: corporate internet banking obtained from another RE; external audits such as VA/PT, IS audit and security review; bulk SMS gateways; procurement of IT hardware or appliances; acquisition of licensed or subscribed software (such as CBS, databases, security solutions) and vendor enhancements to it; OEM maintenance including security patches and bug fixes; applications provided by financial-sector regulators or institutions such as CCIL, NSE and BSE; platforms such as Reuters, Bloomberg and SWIFT; off-the-shelf products such as anti-virus or email licensed with no or minimal customisation; services obtained as a sub-member of a Centralised Payment System from another RE; and business correspondent services, payroll processing and statement printing.
controls.guidance: Use to scope, not to waive: record the exclusion relied on for each vendor outside the MD so materiality classification (2(c)) is auditable. SaaS email or security tools with material customisation or hosting of customer data are not automatically excluded; hosted SaaS is cloud computing under 3(a)(iv)(e). Exclusion from these Directions does not remove other obligations such as CERT-In, DPDP or financial-services outsourcing rules (the 2006 guidelines for banks, the 2017 Directions for NBFCs, both now superseded by the entity-wise Managing Risks in Outsourcing Directions, 2025). The successor exclusion list is NBFC 2025 para 5(2).
evidenceExpected: Vendor register entries marked excluded with the Appendix III item relied upon

controls.title: Vendors not treated as third-party service providers
controls.prose: Indicative, non-exhaustive list of vendors not treated as Third-Party Service Providers under the Directions: vendors providing business services using IT such as business correspondents; payment system operators authorised by RBI under the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007; partnership-based fintechs providing co-branded applications, services or products (treated under outsourcing of financial services instead); fintech data retrieval, validation and verification services such as bank statement analysis, GST returns analysis, vehicle information fetch, digital document execution, and data entry and call-centre services; telecom providers of leased lines and similar transmission infrastructure; and security or audit consultants acting as independent certifiers, auditors or lead implementers.
controls.guidance: Record the exclusion basis per vendor. Co-lending and co-branded fintech partners fall under the financial-services outsourcing and digital lending instructions, so Maxwell should still map them under those instruments rather than dropping them from the inventory.
evidenceExpected: Vendor register entries marked not-TPSP with the Appendix III category relied upon
